items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-01
items.q: The interviewee discusses social organizations (Olympians, Odd Fellows) and does not mention any personal interaction or relationship with Ruth.

ctx.x: Not from the musicians particularly. No, no, I mean the- Oh, the marching groups? The, uh, the social organizations. Oh, yeah. There were, uh, in fact some of the photographs show, in particular show, and as I remember this was a young men's Olympians organization, I think. Yeah. That had both, that had sort of a paramilitary unit, uh, and I think a ladies auxiliary. I'm not sure, so sure about the ladies auxiliary with the Olympians. It may have been, it may have been an odd fellows group.
Yeah, well, they have the household of Ruth, I think, the odd fellows.

But, uh, the, uh, the young men of the Olympians, uh, had a, had a khaki, uh, uniform. Uh-huh. With, uh, a certain, with the officer types carrying sabers. And, uh, uh, although basically they didn't do anything very fancy. As I remember the odd fellows had, had a men's unit which did some fairly elaborate, medium elaborate military type drill. And a ladies organization, the ladies dressed, as I recall, in white two-piece uniforms with a, with a, uh, uh, barracks type cap, I think you'd call it. A build cap.
